Specifically, Your firm changed batch release specifications in response to out-of-specification (OOS) results without providing adequate scientific rationale, and without following formal change control procedures. Review of the OOS log identified at least specification changes made in response to OOS results over 3 years (OOS-0002, OOS-0005-QC, OOS-0009-QC, OOS-0021-QC, OOS-0024-QC, OOS-0030-QC, OOS-0041-QC, OOS-0053-QC, OOS-0055-QC, OOS-0080-QC) allowing substandard batches to be released to the market. For example: A. OOS-0021-QC - [redacted], Lot [redacted] - Deficiencies in OOS-0021-QC Investigation: Your firm explicitly states "”o root causefor the high [redacted] values has been determined" yet proceeded to change the specification and release the batch. However, the specification was widened from [redacted] % to [redacted] % specifically to accommodate the 107.3% failing result. No scientific rationale was provided for wh [redacted] % [redacted] is acceptable when % was previously the upper limit, or what quality attributes are affected by higher [redacted] levels. The investigation committed to "review ofstability data providing proofthat the [redacted] analysis is stable throughout the expiry" yet the batch was released prior to completion of PHASES: Follow-up Completion which remains blank. On, 11/27/2023, the batch was released as "acceptable and safefor consumer use" based on the assertion it "is expected to pass all stability requirements" - an assumption, not verified data. B. OOS-0024-QC - [redacted] Process Validation, Lots [redacted] - Deficiencies in OOS- 0024-QC Investigation: Your firm changed specifications to accommodate the failing process validation batch without investigating why the process cannot meet specifications, modifying the process, or repeating validation with successful batches. Rather than investigating why viscosity exceeded specifications and correcting the process, your firm eliminated the specification without justification for why viscosity is not critical to quality. Your firm justified high [redacted] (0.176% vs. [redacted] % specification) by stating it is "within the USP tolerance of% amount max"; however, the batch failed your firm's established specification. USP maximum is a safety limit, not a quality target. All results being above specification indicates an unaddressed process problem. No investigation was conducted into why the process cannot consistently meet specifications for [redacted], viscosity, and homogeneity. On 01/08/2024 Lot # [redacted] was released for distribution.

Specifically, your firm's complaint handling Standard Operating Procedures SOP NLQA-005 “Product-Customer Complaints” Rev 4 effective 04/01/2025 and SOP NLQA-006_ “Product Complaint Investigation” Rev 4 effective 04/01/2025 lacks sufficient detail regarding investigation requirements, root cause analysis procedures, trending analysis, and corrective and preventive action (CAPA) implementation for product quality complaints. For example, Between 2023 and 2025, the firm received 194 complaints regarding leaking bottles affecting at least 15 different batches, including but not limited to [redacted] (Batch Record# [redacted]) and [redacted] (Batch Record# [redacted]). Leaking/seal complaints increased from 37 in 2023 to 89 in 2024, representing a 140% increase, before decreasing to 68 in 2025. This trend was observable, yet the firm took no investigative action. The firm's response to the leaking bottle complaints consisted solely of replacing the affected product units for consumers without: investigating the underlying cause(s) of the container closure failures, evaluating the impact on affected batch(es) [redacted] (Batch Record# [redacted]) and [redacted] (Batch Record# [redacted]), assessing whether distributed product poses quality or safety concerns and/or implementing corrective actions to prevent recurrence.

Specifically, In WX-SOP-10217: Laboratory Investigation Report Procedure, Section 5.5.9.1, states: "If no root cause is identified through phase 1 and 2 investigations, upon consultation with QA, the investigation may progress to retesting.". Section 5.5.9.5 specifies: "If all results meet specification, are within system suitability and sample acceptance criteria the re-testing can be reported and the original analysis invalidated.". This SOP allows retesting and subsequently invalidate the original results if no root cause has been identified, which is inappropriate. When no clear laboratory error has been identified, the initial results may constitute valid analytical findings that should be reported and considered in the batch release decisions. SEE

Specifically, You have not implemented your documented risk management procedure, Quality Risk Assessment Process SOP MDSPS-B-186 Rev 1 dated 10/21/2024, in the following areas: A. Regulatory Compliance Risk Assessment: The firm failed to conduct risk assessments prior to product distribution to ensure regulatory compliance requirements are met. Products continue to be distributed without appropriate premarket authorization, indicating inadequate risk evaluation of regulatory compliance impacts. B. Product Risk Management Documentation: Risk management documentation is madequate for individual device types, with a single FMEA table applied across all lubricant devices rather than device-specific risk analyses. Risk identification is mcomplete, failing to systematically address environmental, biological, functional, and mechanical hazards as required for comprehensive risk Surveillance Risk Assessment: The complaint handling system lacks risk-based prioritization, treating all complaints with equal severity regardless of potential safety impact. Data aggregation and trend analysis are not performed to identify emerging risks from post-market feedback. D. Supplier and Material Change Risk Assessment: Changes to preservative raw material specifications and suppliers [redacted] were implemented without conducting risk assessments to evaluate potential impacts on device safety and performance. The change control process does not incorporate systematic risk evaluation as required E. Design Change Risk Assessment: Modifications to package size and cap configuration were implemented without risk assessment to determine potential impacts on product safety and effectiveness. Design change controls lack integration with risk management processes. F. Manufacturing Process Change Risk Assessment: Changes to manufacturing batch sizes were implemented without risk-based evaluation of potential impacts on product quality and safety. Process validation gaps in packaging and sealing operations were not identified through risk assessment, resulting in quality issues including leakage and potential contamination risks. This systemic failure to apply risk-based thinking throughout the quality management system demonstrates non-conformance.
